rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fresh re-fire this session against re-hashed body 7bda57b9... (git diff HEAD~1 confirms the ONLY change since the last-judged body is chunk 8 line 59: em-dash sentence split in two: 'This one runs on the screen — watch the list come back rather than typing along.' -> 'This one runs on the screen. Watch the list come back rather than typing along.'). Chunks 0-7 and 9 unchanged from the prior sound PASS; re-verified independently this session (own read of raw lines 1-71, own cross-file greps against diagnose-and-resend.md and site/layouts/curriculum.js) with no new finding. CHANGED REGION, chunk 8 (lines 56-64), weighed specifically per dispatch instruction: 'This one runs on the screen. Watch the list come back rather than typing along.' Neither 'this one' nor 'the list' has an explicit noun antecedent earlier in the sentence -- the immediately preceding clause names only 'the same primitive' (hooks in general) and 'the verifier you built' (a past, already-built hook), neither of which 'this one' can restate without contradiction (a hook already built does not newly 'run on the screen'). Both terms resolve only forward, to `{{prompt:what-packaging-is-1}}` two lines below in the SAME chunk (expanded via `node scripts/expand-md.js`, prompt body ends 'List them.' -- the noun 'list' never appears verbatim before that). This is weaker than the pre-split version: conjoined by an em-dash, 'this one runs on the screen -- watch the list come back' read as one clause whose second half continued the first's momentum toward the prompt block directly under it; split into two sentences, 'the list' now opens a fresh sentence with no antecedent noun of its own, which is the specific risk the dispatch flagged. Weighed against the rule text: the file's own precedent for same-chunk forward pointing is rule 12's carve-out ('same-`##`-chunk use passes... the test is whether the referent sits inside the SAME chunk'), and chunk 8 is four lines total (2 bullets + prompt block + 1 closer) -- short enough that a reader takes in bullet 2 and the prompt block as one glance, not as isolated sequential prose the `##` cut stranded. Harm test (per dispatch preamble): does a reader fail to understand what 'this one' / 'the list' point to? On this chunk's actual visual shape -- the prompt sits two lines under the demonstrative, nothing else competes as a candidate referent -- the answer is no; a single unambiguous candidate sits in view. PASS, but flagged as a materially closer call than the pre-split body: if the maintainer wants a version immune to a stricter reading, 'this one' -> 'the hook below' removes the ambiguity outright without adding a sentence.

Re-run this session: `sed -n '1,71p' curriculum/lectures/what-packaging-is.md | grep -nE "opening lecture|earlier lecture|prior lecture|previous lecture|last lecture|earlier module|prior module|previous module|previous slide|earlier slide"` -> zero hits. All practitioner citations named directly with same-sentence unpacking, never located by file position. Unaffected by the chunk-8 change.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-read this session with the 2026-08-19 generalisation in mind (orientation headers, catalogue entries, and phase/section labels are NOT violations). Chunk 1 'One session, plotted' is a scene-setting title for the chart figure -- reads as a catalogue-entry-shaped label naming its subject (the session, plotted as a chart), close to the generalisation's own example set ('Ralph', 'The numbers'). Chunk 8 'Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste' is an elliptical parallel-structure label (implied 'are'), not a subject-verb claim in the shape of 'Passing is not proof' / 'Gates decay'. Both headers self-carry their chunk under rule 6, and 'Reference and plan' (chunk 2, same file) already carries a maintainer accept-note on the identical structural grounds ('not every header owes a claim'). Filing this as a maintainer-scope corpus question rather than a per-file defect: the 2026-08-19 generalisation's carve-out list (orientation / catalogue / phase-label) may already cover chunk 1 and chunk 8 by function even without a per-file accept-note, in which case this is not a live REVISE at all -- but no accept-note names either header, so the letter of the rule is unresolved. Consistent with the prior instance's finding; unaffected by the chunk-8 body change (the heading itself did not change).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Maintainer call: either extend the carve-out already granted to 'Reference and plan' to cover chunk 1 and chunk 8 by the same function-not-wording test the 2026-08-19 generalisation states, or add a per-header accept-note, or rewrite as claims. Non-blocking either way.
